g.text: ACID and BASE are ends of a dial, not two camps
Real systems sit somewhere along it — and many let you choose per operation.
◀ more coordination, higher latency, lower availability
less coordination, lower latency, higher availability ▶
Atomicity all of it, or none of it
Consistency your declared constraints still hold
(the odd one out — it's your job,
Isolation concurrent txns don't see each
Durability committed means it survives a crash
Soft state replicas may disagree right
Eventually consistent stop writing and they converge
Not a protocol. A description of what you
DynamoDB eventually-consistent reads by default, strong on request
Cassandra consistency chosen per query, by picking R and W
So: not 'is it ACID or BASE?' but 'what does THIS operation need?'
